p01.why: a * b is a prvalue, so the program cannot take its address.

p02.why: A scoped enumeration is not a valid operand of *.

p03.why: float has 24 bits of precision, so 2^24 + 1 rounds back to 2^24 on x86-64; the specification does not say the rounding is to nearest, ties to even, so I used outside knowledge for which neighbor is chosen.

p04.why: Integer division by zero is undefined, and constant evaluation rejects it.

p05.why: INT_MIN / -1 does not fit in int; Clang and GCC reject it during constant evaluation, and EDG 7.0 accepts it.

p06.why: With 24, 53, and 64 bits of precision and each operation rounded on x86-64, adding half an ulp to 1 rounds back to 1 and a full ulp does not; this assumes ties go to even, which the specification does not state.

p07.why: An unscoped enumeration times a double is valid with a deprecation warning, and without -Werror the warning does not stop translation; 2 * 1.5 is 3.0.

p08.why: With -m32 GCC may keep extra precision in the sum, but a cast, an initializer, and a return value round it to 1.0 on every compiler.

p09.why: 65536 * 65537 does not fit in int, and the undefined sanitizer stops the program.

p10.why: Integer division truncates toward zero, and the remainder satisfies the identity, has the sign of the dividend, and is smaller in magnitude than the divisor.

p11.why: All products and quotients are exact.

p12.why: Unsigned products wrap modulo 2 to the width of the type.

p13.why: All the products and quotients are exact in their types.

p14.why: Remainder by zero is undefined and constant evaluation rejects it.

p15.why: double follows IEEE 754 on x86-64, so 1.0 / 0.0 is positive infinity, and -fsanitize=undefined does not stop a floating-point division by zero.

p16.why: % does not accept a floating-point operand.

p17.why: A class without an operator/ or a usable conversion is not a valid operand.

p18.why: The left operand writes i and the right operand reads i without a function call between them; Clang and GCC warn under -Wall and -Werror makes that an error.

p19.why: zero is 0 at run time, so 10 / zero is integer division by zero, which the sanitizer (or the hardware) stops.

p20.why: The order of the two calls is unspecified, the program accepts either order, and 6 * 3 is 18.

p21.why: LLONG_MIN / -1 does not fit; Clang and GCC reject it in long long during constant evaluation, and EDG 7.0 accepts it.

p22.why: *, /, and % share one precedence, group left to right, and bind tighter than +.

p23.why: bool, unsigned char, and the enumeration promote to int, unsigned with long long gives long long, and long long with double gives double.

p24.why: Left-to-right grouping and unary operators binding tighter make every assertion hold.

p25.why: Small integers promote to int, short with long gives long, any integer with float gives float, and -1 * 1u wraps to ~0u.

p26.why: 1e308 * 10 is finite but too large for double; Clang gives infinity, and GCC and EDG reject the constant.

p27.why: Remainders take the sign of the dividend and satisfy the quotient identity.

p28.why: INT_MAX * 2 overflows int, and constant evaluation rejects it.

p29.why: A pointer to member is not a valid operand of *.

p30.why: The result of * is a prvalue, so the program cannot assign to it.

p31.why: With -m32 long cannot hold every unsigned value, so both operands become unsigned long and -1L becomes ULONG_MAX.

p32.why: The program accepts both the rounded and the extra-precision results.

p33.why: Every product wraps modulo the type's range to the asserted value, and the unsigned quotient identity holds.

p34.why: Unscoped enumerations, bool, and char are valid % operands, and 'a' is 97 in UTF-8.

p35.why: INT_MIN % -1 is undefined, and the sanitizer or the hardware exception stops the program.

p36.why: Each mixed operand pair converts to its common type and the values match.

p37.why: The order of the two calls is unspecified, the program accepts either order, and 6 / 3 is 2.

p38.why: An enumeration times a double is deprecated, the compilers warn, and -Werror makes the warning an error.

p39.why: Both short operands promote to int, so -32768 / -1 is 32768 with no overflow.

p40.why: 1e308 / 1e-10 is finite but too large for double; Clang gives infinity, and GCC and EDG reject.

p41.why: INT_MIN % -1 is undefined; Clang and GCC reject it during constant evaluation, and EDG 7.0 accepts it.

p42.why: i++ and the read of i are unsequenced; the compilers warn under -Wall and -Werror makes that an error.

p43.why: The type of nullptr is not a valid operand of *.

p44.why: Multiplying two different enumerations is deprecated, the compilers warn, and -Werror makes the warning an error.

p45.why: On x86-64 long holds every unsigned value, so the common type is long and -1 / 2 truncates to 0.

p46.why: 0 / 0 gives a NaN in each IEEE type, NaN / 0 stays a NaN, and a NaN never compares equal to itself, so bad stays 0.

p47.why: unsigned short promotes to int, 65535 * 65535 does not fit in a 32-bit int, and constant evaluation rejects the overflow.

p48.why: INT_MIN / -1 is undefined, and the sanitizer or the hardware exception stops the program.

p49.why: None of these divides INT_MIN by -1, and every quotient and remainder matches truncation toward zero.

p50.why: Division by zero gives infinities whose sign follows the operand signs, including -0.0, so bad stays 0.

p52.why: A pointer is not a valid operand of *.
